page: Amazon Web Services c1.xlarge is a legacy first-generation compute-optimized instance hosted on the Xen hypervisor. It is configured with an eight-core Intel Xeon E5-2651 v2 processor operating at a base frequency of 1.8 GHz, delivering eight dedicated vCPUs with single-threaded core execution. The architecture lacks support for modern vector and matrix acceleration instructions such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX, though it includes hardware support for AES cryptographic operations. Memory capacity is limited to 7.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an allocation of 0.88 GB per vCPU core. The platform includes 1680 GB of integrated local hard disk drive (HDD) storage, paired with a baseline network bandwidth capacity of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the older architecture and modest clock frequency of the processor. Single-core performance is constrained, as demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 515.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 948.6, both placing in the bottom tier of evaluated systems. Multithreaded execution benefits from the eight dedicated physical cores, reaching a Geekbench multi-core score of 2069.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5469.95. Memory throughput on large 256 MB blocks remains functional at 41.48 GB/sec for reads and 34.05 GB/sec for writes, achieving mid-tier results despite lower cached memory bandwidth. Compression, static web throughput, and in-memory operations like Redis SET show reduced processing throughput.

The instance exhibits a distinct hardware tradeoff: high local rotational storage capacity coupled with dedicated physical compute cores, offset by restrictive memory density and legacy compute efficiency. In modern infrastructure deployments, this profile is less cost-effective for pure compute-intensive or memory-bound tasks. The c1.xlarge remains best suited for legacy batch jobs, background processing pipelines, distributed log parsing, or basic sequential data extraction where vast HDD scratch capacity is prioritized over high per-core execution speeds.
description: Amazon Web Services c1.xlarge is a legacy first-generation compute-optimized instance operating on the Xen hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon E5-2651 v2 processor clocked at 1.8 GHz, paired with 7.0 GB of system memory and 1680 GB of local HDD storage. Network throughput operates at a baseline of 1 Gbps. With an allocation of 0.88 GB of memory per core and an instruction set lacking AVX and AVX-512 capabilities, execution performance in modern benchmarks ranks in the lower tiers, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 515.0 and multi-core score of 2069.0. PassMark database tests achieve average throughput, supported by decent uncached memory bandwidth. Due to its combination of dedicated physical cores and large magnetic storage volume, the c1.xlarge is suitable for legacy batch workloads, basic sequential file extraction, and non-critical data ingestion tasks.
